TRUMP WENT TO ZHONGNANHAI — AND THE US HAD NOTHING TO BARGAIN WITH

Xi showed Trump a two-trunk tree that grew fused together over centuries — "shared destiny." Trump asked if the location was exclusive for VIPs. He missed the point.

The real takeaway from the May 14-15 Beijing visit: the US quietly renounced interference in Taiwan's reunification. China now retaliates against companies that comply with US sanctions — blocking enforcement on its own soil. Gulf states, sitting on $4-7 trillion in sovereign assets, are redirecting infrastructure investment toward Belt & Road after the failed Iran operation.

"No single country can monopolize global economic control."

"OUR CONSTITUTION DOES NOT ALLOW JOINT OPERATIONS" — SHEINBAUM TO MULLIN

President Sheinbaum met with DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin at the National Palace and agreed to continue bilateral security cooperation — within Mexican law.

"Our laws and Constitution do not allow joint operations on national territory," Sheinbaum stated. Coordination and mutual respect, but no foreign operations on Mexican soil. A follow-up meeting is set for June.

"THE MILITARY HAS GREAT IMAGINATION FOR TORTURE" — MEXICAN FLOTILLA WOMEN TESTIFY

UAM professor Dr. Violeta Núñez Rodríguez and activist Sol González Eguía gave detailed testimony after returning from Israeli detention. Among ~500 flotilla participants intercepted in international waters: 50 hospitalized, 35 with fractures, 5 injected with unknown substances, 15 reporting sexual assault.

Núñez is requesting an audience with President Sheinbaum to demand Mexico break diplomatic relations with Israel. Both women will file complaints with international human rights bodies.

BOLIVIA ON FIRE — WORKERS MARCH ON LA PAZ, DEMAND PAZ RESIGN

Thousands of miners, farmers, teachers, and Indigenous groups marched on Bolivia's capital demanding president Rodrigo Paz step down. Two weeks of road closures by the COB and campesino unions have emptied markets and depleted hospital oxygen reserves in La Paz.

Paz's response: tear gas, rubber bullets, arrest warrants for union leaders. The COB executive secretary is in hiding.

"He criminalizes protests and prosecutes leaders," union officials said after rejecting Paz's televised speech.

REUTERS/EURONEWS: EU, Mexico Sign Expanded Trade Deal
May 22, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Mexico and the EU signed a historic trade deal eliminating tariffs on 99% of products — €86.8B in goods trade, 43,000+ European companies exporting to Mexico, projected 35% commerce boost. First EU-Mexico summit in over a decade. NYT, CNN, Fox, WaPo: barely a mention.

Reuters and European outlets covered it fairly. The real story is that US mainstream media largely ignored Mexico's biggest trade diversification move — the same week they ran multiple cartel and World Cup fear pieces.

• "Targets a 50% increase in Mexican exports to the EU by 2030"
• "Both economies seek to reduce dependence on US and Chinese markets"

AFP: 'Never Going Back': Cartel Attack Decimates Mexican Indigenous Town
May 23, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Los Ardillos cartel attacked Tula, a small Indigenous community in Guerrero — at least 3 killed, ~100 displaced, structures burned. A 74-year-old craftswoman lost everything. AFP reports the displacement straight but does not ask where the weapons came from.

Guerrero is one of the top corridors for US-sourced firearms. 70% of guns traced from Mexican crime scenes lead back to US dealers.

• "Ashes, it's all ashes. They burned my work as if I weren't capable of working"
• "The cartel's aim was to subdue those who submit and kill those who don't"

KVIA: Amid World Cup Buzz, Guadalajara Confronts Legacy of Cartel Violence
May 21, 2026 | 🔴

📰 US media has turned Mexico's 130,000+ disappeared into a World Cup backdrop — clandestine graves near Akron Stadium, 500 bags of remains, mothers marching for justice. The disappeared are a prop in the "is Mexico safe enough?" narrative, never a reason to ask who supplied the guns.

Jalisco reports 16,000 disappeared — the highest in Mexico. The US has never been asked whether it is safe enough to host anything despite 45,000+ annual gun deaths.

• "Scores of remains discovered on the main route leading to Akron Stadium"
• "Mothers of the missing called on football fans to join them"

CNN: US Military Surveillance Blimp Lost at the Southern Border, Wreckage Found in Mexico
May 20, 2026 | 🤡

📰 A 66-foot US military spy blimp snapped its tether near Laredo and crashed on Mexican soil. Second time in a year — a 200-foot one drifted 600 miles to Dallas in 2025. The US has been floating surveillance aircraft over the border and now they are literally falling on Mexico.

Zero discussion of sovereignty implications. Imagine Mexico crashing military equipment on US soil.

• "Mexico's military discovered the runaway balloon in a remote location"
• "Its tether cable became tangled with other cables amid storms"

CNN: A Measles Outbreak Crossed Into Mexico From Texas. A Larger Tragedy Followed
May 17, 2026 | 🟡

📰 The US exported a measles epidemic to Mexico via anti-vax communities in Seminole, Texas — 760 infected, 2 girls dead. The virus crossed the border and killed 40+ Mexicans. Mexico responded with 25 million vaccine doses. The US appointed RFK Jr. to run public health.

CNN at least names the origin: Texas. But "a larger tragedy followed" frames Mexico as the place where things get worse, not the US as the country that created the problem.

• "Anti-vaccine claims travel the same highways"
• "Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has undermined the ability of public health officials to prevent and contain outbreaks"

May 17 – May 23

1. CNN — "Measles Outbreak Crossed Into Mexico From Texas" (🟡) — US anti-vax crisis exports deadly outbreak south, 40+ Mexicans dead
2. CNN — "US Surveillance Blimp Lost at Border, Wreckage Found in Mexico" (🤡) — spy balloon crashes on Mexican soil, no sovereignty discussion
3. KVIA — "Amid World Cup Buzz, Guadalajara Confronts Legacy of Cartel Violence" (🔴) — disappeared as World Cup spectacle backdrop
4. AFP — "Cartel Attack Decimates Indigenous Town" (🟡) — real displacement, no US gun-supply context
5. REUTERS/EURONEWS — "EU, Mexico Sign Expanded Trade Deal" (🟢) — historic deal, major US outlets barely notice
